title: Normalization of the localized pullback on arbitrary complexes
statement: Fix schemes X,Y, f:X→Y, ring sheaves RY,RX, coefficient identification c, Global datum g, V in Y.ProEt and Local datum l as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction-data]. Let G,H be the ordinary restrictions on Y and X, F the global ordinary module pullback and K the local one. Define gamma:G K→F H to be the inverse adjunction mate of l.ordinaryDirectImage.hom using the actual module adjunctions. Write theta=l.pullback.inv, and for a complex P let bFH(P):H_D(F_D(QP))≅Q(H(FP)) and bGK(P):K_D(G_D(QP))≅Q(K(GP)) be the composites of the supplied exact-functor localization factors. For every cochain complex P of Mod(RY), theta(QP) followed by bFH(P).hom equals bGK(P).hom followed by Q(gamma applied termwise to P). This assertion involves no tensor products or K-flatness.

proof.text: Identify Operation.rightComparison with the canonical cochain unit rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ; the mapHomotopyCategoryFactors component is identity. Its naturality gives a natural transformation on all complexes. Apply derived_unit_cochain to the actual module adjunction and use naturality to obtain the normalized Hom equation for any chain map out of the termwise pullback.

source.place: Tags 0DVC and 09T5; cochain normalization of the canonical derived adjunction unit.

proof.text: Regard the two right-square normalization composites as natural transformations on complexes. For arbitrary I choose a K-injective resolution j:I→J. Restriction is exact, so the target functor maps j to an isomorphism. At J the supplied directImage_representative, postcomposed with the right-derived image of the restriction factor, gives equality by cancellation. Naturality and cancellation of the invertible target map j prove equality at I.

source.place: Tags 07A6 and 08FI; normalization on K-injective resolutions and naturality.

proof.text: The supplied mate_counit identifies the mate of pullback.inv with directImage.hom by the local Hom bijection. The inverse mate unit identity identifies the ordinary transpose of gamma in each degree. Apply the local derived Hom bijection to both proposed maps, use the normalized unit and Hom equations and the right-square normalization just established, and move the restriction factor through the ordinary unit by naturality. The transposes coincide, hence so do the maps.

lean.statement:
theorem localPullbackNormalization
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (R_Y : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (R_X : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (c : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R_Y ≅ R_X)
    (g : Global f R_Y R_X c) (V : Y.ProEt)
    (l : Local f R_Y R_X c g V) :
    letI := l.restrictionYAdditive
    letI := l.restrictionXAdditive
    ∀ P : CochainComplex (Mod R_Y) ℤ,
      l.pullback.inv.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫
        l.restrictionX.model.functor.map (g.operation.leftModel.factors.hom.app P) ≫
        l.restrictionX.model.factors.hom.app
          ((g.operation.pullback.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) =
      l.operation.left.map (l.restrictionY.model.factors.hom.app P) ≫
        l.operation.leftModel.factors.hom.app
          ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u + 1}
            ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology Y)
              (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj R_Y) V).mapHomologicalComplex
              (.up ℤ) |>.obj P) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map
          ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex (localOrdinaryPullbackSquare l) (.up ℤ)).app P)
